newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia revises GDP growth upward to 6.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia revises GDP growth upward to 6.5 percent.

text.p: Finance Minister Keat Chhon said on Monday that Cambodia's economic growth for 1996 had been revised up to 6.5 percent after a review of the country's performance last year.

Keat Chhon said that in meetings with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), his ministry determined that gross domestic product (GDP) growth was 6.5 percent in 1996, rather than the 6.0 percent previously reported by the government.
The IMF is in Cambodia reviewing the government's fiscal performance and policies to determine the fate of $40 million in loans.
Keat Chhon attributed the revision to agricultural growth, which he said was better than initially reported despite heavy flooding late last year.
"This means the economy is quite resilient," he told reporters after opening a seminar for finance officials. "We have scored a success in microeconomic stability," he said.
The new figure brought GDP growth closer to the government's 1996 goal of 7.0 percent, although it still fell slightly short of the mark because of the flooding, Keat Chhon said.
Per capita GDP now stands at under $300, almost triple the $119 level three years ago. Inflation was 7.5 percent in 1996.
